entries.note: Smith 2016 PubMed (PMID 26870941, epub 2016-02-12): quote verbatim in abstract. Topical gsk-2981278 ointment, unselected. Untested opener fine; retrodiction false sits oddly beside entry 2's true (same public date).

SID 2017 abstract (academia.edu copy) has the quote verbatim; 4% topical plaques. Explants public Feb 2016 after Vitae's Sep/Nov 2015 whole-blood IL-17 suppression (same target, action), so retrodiction true; failed to reproduce, contra holds.

Protocol (Amd 2, 21-Dec-2017) quote verbatim; AGN-242428 'formerly VTP-43742', oral. Vitae release 18 Nov 2015 read: >90% ex vivo whole-blood IL-17A suppression over 24 h in volunteers (SAD Sep 2015). Year 2015 right.

Smith 2016 strength sentence is full-text (abstract read, prior check saw verbatim). Topical gsk-2981278; model text matches gsk-srica-human-skin. Untested holds (skin exposure never measured); lacks untested_reason (not_measured).

Protocol IC90 exposure sentence verbatim. Nov 2015 release: >90% suppression sustained 24 h in all but lowest cohort, so the model's IC90 target was reached in 2015. Oral VTP-43742; margin_stated false right.

23% epidermal-thickness quote in Smith 2016 (full text, prior check verbatim). Topical gsk-2981278, IMQ mouse. Public Feb 2016, before VTP-43742's Mar 2016 patient efficacy result, so not a retrodiction; untested opener fine.

entries.rule: CHECKER_BRIEF 3: trial source attributes result to conditions the model never tested -> untested; DRAFTER dose table: target never reached -> efficacy untested
entries.note: Quote verbatim in SID abstract; primary endpoint infiltrate thickness; topical right. Authors attribute the null to no dermal penetration, small test fields, short duration, and engagement 2 shows IL-17 unmoved: target not reached, so efficacy untested; miss counted once in engagement.
entries.adjudication_note: CHECKER_BRIEF 3 and DRAFTER dose table: trial authors attribute the null to no dermal penetration, and plaque biopsies show IL-17 unmoved (engagement contra), so the IMQ mouse efficacy prediction was never tested; miss counted once in engagement.

entries.note: Gooderham 2025 abstract quote verbatim; co-primary PASI75 and sPGA 0/1 both met, in note. Harcken online 2021-01-05 (abstract only) post-dates VTP-43742 Mar 2016 PASI result, so retro right. Oral BI 730357. Judgement prose still says 'so same'.
Protocol IB sentence verbatim. Registry: AGN-242428 oral capsules, plaque psoriasis, whyStopped 'safety reason'. Drug, route, population right; tox unpublished, so untested/unpublished stands.

missing: Engagement, VTP-43742: a peer-reviewed healthy-volunteer PK/PD paper ('Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of VTP-43742, a RORγt inhibitor, in normal healthy volunteers', ResearchGate 366800762, c. 2022-23) is a tier-1 source for the whole-blood IL-17 readout; it does not predate the 2021 registry date, so it adds no status change. Not opened.

Efficacy patient_trials: NCT03835481 (BI 730357 long-term extension) TERMINATED 'Due to company decision', results posted 2022-11-18. This was a program stop, not an efficacy failure under decision 4 ('Failed' ≠ development stopped).
Safety: NCT03339999 registry gives whyStopped 'safety reason' (verified). The draft says so, but no source says what the safety signal was.
rule_questions: When the topical drug fails the engagement readout in the same biopsied field, does the efficacy cell become untested (target not reached, decision 4 row 1) even though the engagement model, not a PK model, set the target? The dose table is written for exposure. The draft scored engagement and efficacy both contra, so one failure counted twice.

Engagement entry 3: the 'model' (human whole-blood ex vivo IL-17 assay) and the human readout (the same assay on dosed subjects' blood) are the same measurement. Does a human ex-vivo assay whose own readout is repeated in dosed humans count as a model prediction that can turn back a contra, or is it close to tautological?
